clips.send: Reflecting telescope. Uses mirrors to gather light. A curved (concave) mirror at the bottom reflects light up to a focus. A small flat mirror sends the light out the side to the eyepiece (a Newtonian design, invented by Isaac Newton in 1668). Mirrors can be made huge, so all the largest telescopes are reflectors. A bigger mirror collects more light and shows fainter objects.

clips.send: Space telescope. Observes from above the atmosphere. Earth’s atmosphere blurs starlight and blocks most infrared, ultraviolet and X-ray light. Space telescopes orbit above the air: Hubble (1990) sees visible and ultraviolet light; the James Webb Space Telescope (2021) sees infrared; Chandra sees X-rays. Hubble uses mirrors too: light bounces off a 2.4 m primary mirror and a small secondary mirror before reaching its cameras.

clips.send: 1990. Hubble Space Telescope. Hubble is launched into an orbit more than 500 km up, above the blurring atmosphere. It helped measure the age of the universe.

clips.send: 2019. Chang’e 4 on the Moon’s far side. Chang’e 4 makes the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon, and its rover Yutu-2 explores the surface.
clips.text: 2019. Chang’e 4 on the Moon’s far side. Chang’e 4 makes the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon, and its rover Yutu-2 explores the surface.

clips.send: Refracting telescope. Uses lenses to bend light. A big convex lens at the front (the objective) bends light so it comes together at a focus. A small eyepiece lens at the back magnifies the image. In 1610 Galileo used a small refractor to discover four moons of Jupiter. Big lenses sag and blur colours, so refractors cannot be made very large.

clips.send: Common mix-up: A telescope’s most important job is not magnifying. It is collecting light. A wider mirror gathers more light, the way a bigger bucket catches more rain.

clips.send: 1997. First Mars rover. Sojourner, a rover the size of a microwave oven, rolls across Mars as part of the Mars Pathfinder mission.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Rockets do not drop stages because they are broken. Empty tanks are dead weight; getting rid of them lets the remaining fuel speed up a lighter rocket.

clips.send: 2021. Perseverance and Ingenuity. The Perseverance rover lands on Mars to collect rock samples, and the small Ingenuity helicopter makes the first powered flight on another planet.

clips.send: 1977. Voyager 1 and 2. The twin Voyager probes launch to visit the giant planets. In 2012 Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to reach interstellar space.
clips.text: 1977. Voyager 1 & 2. The twin Voyager probes launch to visit the giant planets. In 2012 Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to reach interstellar space.

clips.send: Nose cone (fairing). Protects the satellite through the air. A streamlined shell that protects the payload from air rushing past and from heating. Once the rocket is above most of the atmosphere, it splits in two and falls away. Dropping it early saves weight.

clips.send: Radio telescope. Catches radio waves from space. A giant metal dish reflects radio waves to a receiver at its focus. Radio waves pass through clouds and the atmosphere, so radio telescopes can work day and night and in cloudy weather. China’s FAST in Guizhou is 500 m across, one of the largest single-dish radio telescopes ever built.

clips.send: Second stage. Speeds up to orbital speed. Ignites after the first stage drops away, high above most of the air. Tips the rocket over so it builds up sideways speed: about 28,000 km/h (7.8 km/s) for a low orbit. Its engine is designed to work in the vacuum of space.

clips.send: Atmosphere. Lets some light through, blocks the rest. Visible light and radio waves pass through the air to reach the ground. Most infrared, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma-ray light is absorbed before it reaches the ground. That is why we put many telescopes in space, or on high, dry mountaintops.

clips.send: Launch pad. Where the journey starts. Holds the rocket upright and supplies fuel, power and data before launch. Many launch sites are near the equator or face east over an ocean: Earth’s spin gives rockets a free eastward push, and spent stages fall into the sea. In the U.S., Cape Canaveral in Florida is a famous launch site; China uses sites such as Wenchang on Hainan Island.

clips.send: 2012. Curiosity lands on Mars. The car-sized Curiosity rover lands in Gale Crater and finds evidence that Mars once had lakes of liquid water.

clips.send: First stage (booster). Lifts the rocket off the ground. The biggest and heaviest part: mostly fuel and oxygen tanks, with powerful engines at the bottom. It burns for only a few minutes and pushes the rocket through the thick lower atmosphere. When its tanks are empty it separates and falls away. Some boosters today fly back and land so they can be reused.

clips.send: 整流罩。穿过大气时保护卫星。流线型的外壳，保护里面的载荷不受高速气流和气动加热的伤害。火箭飞到大部分大气层之上后，整流罩一分为二并脱落。提前抛掉它可以减轻质量。

clips.send: 发射台。旅程的起点。发射前它支撑着火箭，并为火箭加注燃料、供电和传输数据。许多发射场靠近赤道或东面临海：地球自转能免费给向东发射的火箭“推一把”，而且分离的残骸会落入大海。美国佛罗里达州的卡纳维拉尔角是著名的发射场；中国有海南文昌等发射场。

clips.send: 容易混淆：火箭抛掉一级并不是因为坏了。空燃料箱是“累赘”，扔掉后剩下的燃料只需推动更轻的火箭，速度能更快。

clips.send: 第二级。加速到轨道速度。第一级分离后点火，此时已经在大部分空气之上。它让火箭逐渐转向水平方向，积累巨大的横向速度：进入近地轨道约需 28,000 千米/时（7.8 千米/秒）。它的发动机专门为真空环境设计。

clips.send: 大气层。让一部分光通过，挡住其他的。可见光和无线电波可以穿过大气到达地面。大部分红外线、紫外线、X 射线和伽马射线在到达地面前就被吸收了。所以我们把很多望远镜送上太空，或者建在又高又干燥的山顶上。

clips.send: 第一级（助推级）。把火箭推离地面。火箭最大最重的部分，主要是燃料箱和氧化剂箱，底部装着强大的发动机。它只工作几分钟，推动火箭穿过稠密的低层大气。燃料用完后它就分离掉落。如今有些助推级能飞回来着陆，重复使用。

clips.send: 2021。毅力号与机智号。毅力号火星车登陆火星采集岩石样本，小直升机机智号完成了人类在另一颗行星上的首次动力飞行。

clips.send: 1990。哈勃空间望远镜。哈勃被送入 500 多千米高的轨道，避开了让图像模糊的大气。它帮助科学家测定了宇宙的年龄。

clips.send: 反射望远镜。用镜子收集光。底部的凹面镜把光反射会聚到焦点。一块小平面镜把光从侧面送到目镜（牛顿式设计，由牛顿于 1668 年发明）。镜子可以做得非常大，所以世界上最大的望远镜都是反射望远镜。镜面越大，收集的光越多，能看到越暗的天体。

clips.send: 折射望远镜。用透镜使光弯折（折射）。前端的大凸透镜（物镜）使光线折射，会聚到一个焦点。后端的小目镜把像放大。1610 年，伽利略用一架小折射望远镜发现了木星的四颗卫星。大透镜会下垂，还会产生色差，所以折射望远镜不能做得很大。

clips.send: 1977。旅行者 1 号和 2 号。两个旅行者号探测器发射升空，飞掠巨行星。2012 年，旅行者 1 号成为第一个进入星际空间的人造物体。

clips.send: 射电望远镜。接收来自太空的无线电波。巨大的金属“锅”把无线电波反射到焦点处的接收器。无线电波能穿过云层和大气，所以射电望远镜白天黑夜、阴天都能工作。位于贵州的中国天眼 FAST 口径 500 米，是有史以来最大的单口径射电望远镜之一。

clips.send: 2019。嫦娥四号登陆月球背面。嫦娥四号实现人类首次在月球背面软着陆，玉兔二号月球车开始巡视探测。

clips.send: 2012。好奇号登陆火星。汽车大小的好奇号火星车降落在盖尔撞击坑，发现火星曾经有液态水湖泊的证据。

clips.send: 空间望远镜。在大气层之上观测。地球大气会让星光变模糊，还会挡住大部分红外线、紫外线和 X 射线。空间望远镜在大气层之上运行：哈勃（1990 年）观测可见光和紫外线；詹姆斯·韦布空间望远镜（2021 年）观测红外线；钱德拉观测 X 射线。哈勃也用镜子：光先被 2.4 米的主镜反射，再经过小副镜，才到达相机。
